task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: impact of lineup changes on shot selection
sample size and power for lineup-level analysis
selection bias due to substitution patterns

historical_evidence.finding: Observed a decline in pull-up shots with exposure that disappeared when lineup fixed effects were removed, suggesting the effect was due to shooter-level confounding rather than a true lineup effect.
Reproduced excess in published suppression studies was small and asymmetric, with drift and exposure sparsity limiting the validity of the effect.
Double-suppression stacking (POST_UP then PUTBACK) did not produce additive effects; sample size and implementation issues limited conclusions.
Penalty-state adaptation contrasts were not distinct from placebo contrasts, and standard errors were not reported, leaving the effect unclear.

failed_approaches.why: artifact due to construction/selection flaw, confounding, placebo dependence
artifact due to drift, exposure sparsity, selection/regression to the mean, mechanical floor, placebo dependence

evidence_establishes: Confounding and placebo dependence are common pitfalls in studies that attribute lineup changes to performance effects.
Exposure sparsity and drift can inflate apparent effects when analyzing rare events.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix in a way that reflects personnel effects.
own_inferences: The data set includes substitution intervals and defensive matchup minutes, but linking these to shot mix at the possession level will require careful alignment and may suffer from limited exposure for many lineups.
Defensive lineup changes and game context (score, period, clock) are potential confounders that need to be controlled for or balanced.
uncertainties: No prior study directly examined shot mix shifts due to offensive lineup changes using the same data structure.
The granularity of defensive matchup minutes may be insufficient to fully control for defensive personnel effects.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved studies do not directly address the question, but they highlight methodological pitfalls that are relevant.

blocking_constraints.text: Defensive lineup and game context may confound the relationship between offensive lineup and shot mix.
Placebo play types often show similar patterns, indicating potential artifacts.
Many specific offensive lineups occur infrequently, limiting statistical power.

prior_work.summary: No prior study in this repository has directly tested whether changing the offensive five alters shot mix to detect personnel effects.

risks.text: Defensive matchups and game state may drive observed shot mix changes.
Similar patterns in unrelated play types suggest artifacts.
Limited exposure of many lineups reduces power.
Shot mix may be measured inconsistently across possessions.

design.estimand: Effect of offensive lineup composition on shot mix (percentage of shots taken from each distance band).
design.sample: All possessions with a documented offensive lineup change within the same game and period.
design.power: Not achievable with current exposure distribution; sample size insufficient for many lineups.
design.controls: Fixed effects for defensive lineup, game context (score, period, clock), and player-level characteristics.
design.falsification: Test the same estimand on unrelated play types (e.g., fastbreak points) to check for artifacts.
design.multiplicity: Apply Holm-Bonferroni correction across distance bands.
design.decision_rule: Reject null if p<0.05 after correction; otherwise fail to reject.
